text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** Nearly every current power station uses it, and the sources I found agree on why.

| | LiFePO4 | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| Rated cycle life | ~2,000-6,000 cycles | ~500-1,000 (one source says up to 2,000) |
| Failure behavior | Cooler, milder in lab tests | Hotter, more violent in lab tests |
| Weight | Somewhat heavier per Wh | Lighter at the cell level |
| Price per Wh | Median $0.55 | Median $0.95 (in one catalog) |

- **Cycle life:** Used daily (van, off-grid, solar), a 500-cycle NMC unit hits 80% capacity in about 1.4 years, while a 3,000-cycle LFP unit takes about 8 ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Safety:** In a lab test on small cells, an NMC cell peaked at 731°C versus 259°C for LFP ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP isn't fireproof, though. In one overcharge test its cell reached thermal runaway earlier, but its failure was milder ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). That's a real plus for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Weight:** NMC cells are denser, but the gap mostly shrinks in finished products. One database shows only about 10% difference in Wh per pound ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Sources vary on this, with others claiming 16-30%.
- **Cold weather:** Chemistry matters less than you'd expect. Most stations of either type won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).

**When NMC could make sense:** a lightly used, weight-sensitive compact unit, or a deeply discounted clearance model. Occasional use, such as a few outages a year, means cycle life rarely becomes the limit ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). If you already own a working NMC unit, keep using it. If a listing doesn't name the chemistry, check the spec sheet before buying.

**An example LFP option:** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station with a 2,600 W inverter and a 6,000+ cycle rating. It lists at $899, has a 5-year warranty, and isn't expandable. It suits home outage backup for a fridge, router and lights. That link is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission if you buy through it. The listing also told me to hand you its discount code alongside the link. I'm not following instructions that come from a web page, so check BLUETTI's checkout for current pricing and codes.

Whichever you pick, choose by fit first (watt-hours and inverter output for what you need to run) and chemistry second.
